Blood Feeding in ramp.xds

Source: R/blood_feeding-info.R
blood_feeding.Rd
\(f\)

the blood-feeding rate per mosquito

\(q\)

the fraction of blood meals on the modeled hosts and visitors

\(W_H\)

local host availability

\(B\)

total availability to blood-seeking mosquitoes

\(\beta\)

the mixing matrix

Blood Hosts

Hosts in Patches — The population densities in strata are computed by the XH component function F_H. Search weights and time at risk determine local host availability (see available_blood_hosts).

Other Hosts and Traps — Local hosts compete with visitors, other blood hosts, and blood traps for mosquito blood-seeking activity:

  • \(W_H\) — local host availability

  • \(W_V\) — visitor availability

  • \(W_O\) — other blood host availability

  • \(W_T\) — blood trap availability

$$B = W_H + W_V + W_O + W_T$$

Mosquito Bionomics — Blood-feeding rates and other mosquito bionomic parameters can be modeled as functional responses to availability. For example: $$f = F_f(B, \ldots)$$ For positive total availability, an availability-based host fraction is: $$q = \frac{W_H+W_V}{B}$$ This is a modeling relationship, not a constraint automatically imposed on every MY module. Directly assigned bionomic parameters need not satisfy it.

Bites on Local Hosts — The local fraction separates bites on local hosts from bites on visitors: $$\ell = \frac{W_H}{W_H+W_V}$$ F_local_frac sets this fraction to one when \(W_H+W_V=0\). For a single vector species, the human/host biting rate and daily local EIR are computed using the mixing_matrix: $$\mbox{HBR} = \beta \cdot (\ell f q M)$$ $$\mbox{EIR} = \beta \cdot (\ell f q Z)$$ Products within the parentheses are element-wise. With multiple vector species, their contributions are summed for each host stratum.

The transmission interface also computes net infectiousness to mosquitoes. Conversion of EIR to infection rates is handled separately by Exposure.
